questions.prompt: What is a sound performance or deployment practice?
options: Assume native compiler speedups guarantee faster application runtime.
Publish source maps and secrets indiscriminately.
Measure a baseline, run type checks/tests/builds, inspect runtime metrics, and prepare rollback/diagnostic controls.
questions.answer_key: Measure a baseline, run type checks/tests/builds, inspect runtime metrics, and prepare rollback/diagnostic controls.
questions.explanation: Compiler performance, application runtime performance and deployment reliability are different concerns.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Performance Profiling”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with build and type-checking times and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with build and type-checking times and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Build and type-checking times”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Performance Profiling”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check runtime profiling, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume separating compiler performance from application performance is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check runtime profiling, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Runtime profiling”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
